newsitem.title: UK: UK shares jump into record territory before budget.
newsitem.headline: UK shares jump into record territory before budget.

text.p: Britain's FTSE share index opened sharply higher ahead of Tuesday's budget, setting an all-time record high on the back of a surge in U.S. stocks overnight.
The FTSE 100 index was up 28.3 points at 4,082.9 by 0850 GMT, after peaking at 4,094.4 soon after the official opening of trade.

The previous FTSE record was 4,073.2, set on October 21. Gainers outweighed losers by nine times, led by U.S.-quoted FTSE heavyweights Glaxo-Wellcome and SmithKline Beecham, and banking stocks like HSBC Holdings.
The Dow surged 76 points on Monday, led by bank stocks and a late rally in Philip Morris, to breeze past the 6500 level for the first time ever.
This sharp rise was the biggest one day points gain for the U.S. market since August and the bulk of the rally came after the London markets had closed.
Traders said hopes for a "prudent" non-inflationary budget coupled with the latest record in New York had propelled stocks forward.
But as UK shares drifted back from initial peaks activity was seen waning and caution setting in ahead of the 1530 GMT budget speech.
